domain: Seoul in depth (neighborhoods, culture/history, markets, experiences, Seoul lodging) and Seoul-based day trips
research_note: The session's web-search budget ran out partway through. Time-sensitive items (Bukchon curfew, Hangang Bus, JSA, Namsan gondola, jjimjilbang closures, palace night programs, Silver Grass Festival, palace fee changes, museum hours, Seoul Sky and N Seoul Tower prices) were checked against 2026 sources. Standing facts (palace hours, most admission fees, coordinates) come from earlier knowledge and are marked medium or low confidence. Lodging prices are estimates built from HotelsCombined/Trip.com snapshots taken in Oct 2026, which mostly quote rates for 2 guests, so check them on Agoda, Booking or Trip.com with 3 adults entered.

places.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
places.summary: Main Joseon palace, built in 1395. Gwanghwamun gate, changing of the guard (10:00 and 14:00, not on Tuesdays), Geunjeongjeon throne hall, Gyeonghoeru pavilion on its pond, and Hyangwonjeong. The National Palace Museum and the National Folk Museum are on the grounds.
places.why: The 'big temple-complex' day, like Kamakura's Tsurugaoka Hachimangu but on an imperial scale. Rent hanbok and you get in free and get great photos.
places.autumn_note: Maples and ginkgos around Hyangwonjeong and Gyeonghoeru usually turn in late Oct to early Nov, so Oct 17-24 is early color. The fall Starlight Tour (별빛야행) runs to Oct 24, with foreigner-only sessions Oct 21-24.
places.time_needed: 2.5-3 h (4 h with both on-site museums)
places.hours: Mar-May and Sep-Oct 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00). The regular night opening ran Sep 2 - Oct 2, 2026 and has ended.
places.cost_note: Adults 3,000. Free if wearing hanbok and on the last Wednesday of the month (Oct 28 falls after the trip). A fee rise has been announced for Jan 2027 (new rates due in November), so Oct 2026 is still 3,000.
places.booking: Walk-up ticket. The Starlight Tour (60,000) needs pre-booking: Ticketlink for general sessions, Creatrip for the Oct 21-24 foreigner sessions (listed as sold out on Oct 6; watch for cancellations, which are free up to 3 days before).
places.tips: Arrive at 09:00 or after 15:30 to avoid tour groups. Walk out the north gate toward Cheong Wa Dae and Samcheong-dong, or west into Seochon. The palace is closed Tuesday, so put it on another day.

places.name: Changdeokgung Palace and Secret Garden (Huwon)
places.summary: UNESCO-listed secondary palace with a 78-acre wooded rear garden (Huwon): Buyongji pond, Aeryeonji, Ongnyucheon stream and Yeongyeongdang. The garden can only be seen on a guided tour.
places.why: The closest Seoul gets to a Kamakura or Kyoto temple garden: a quiet wooded garden with pavilions over ponds. This is the best autumn palace.
places.autumn_note: Huwon foliage usually peaks late Oct to mid Nov, so expect early-to-mid color in the week of Oct 19. The Moonlight Tour (달빛기행) ends Oct 17. Its foreigner-only sessions ended Oct 11.
places.time_needed: Palace 1 h + Secret Garden tour 90 min
places.hours: Sep-Oct about 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00). English Secret Garden tours about 10:30, 11:30, 14:30, 15:30 (sources differ, so check the day's schedule).
places.cost_note: Palace 3,000 + Huwon 5,000 = 8,000. Hanbok wearers get free palace entry but must still pay for the garden tour (verify).
places.booking: Huwon: about 50 online seats per tour released 6 days ahead at 10:00 KST on the royal palaces site (ticket.khs.go.kr). They sell out fast in autumn. The rest are sold on site the same day, so arrive at opening.
places.tips: Book Huwon the moment the window opens. For a Wed Oct 21 visit, book Thu Oct 15 at 10:00 KST (Wed Oct 14, 21:00 US Eastern). Pair it with Changgyeonggung next door (an internal gate connects them) and Ikseon-dong for lunch.
places.image_query: Buyongji pond Changdeokgung Secret Garden autumn

places.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
places.summary: Palace linked to Changdeokgung, with Chundangji pond and the 1909 Daeonsil glass greenhouse. It is open until 21:00, so it doubles as an evening stroll.
places.why: A quiet, cheap evening palace walk next to Jongmyo and Ikseon-dong.
places.autumn_note: The trees around Chundangji pond are a strong late-Oct foliage spot.
places.cost_note: 1,000. Free in hanbok.
places.tips: Go just before sunset (about 17:50 that week) and stay into the dusk lighting.

places.name: Deoksugung Palace and Stone-wall Road
places.summary: Palace that mixes Joseon and Western styles (Seokjojeon), with a changing of the guard at Daehanmun. Next to it is the Deoksugung Doldam-gil stone-wall road and the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Deoksugung branch.
places.why: Easy to reach from a Myeongdong or Seoul Station base, and good at night. The stone-wall road is the classic autumn ginkgo walk.
places.autumn_note: The ginkgos on the stone-wall road usually turn gold in late Oct to early Nov.
places.cost_note: 1,000. Free in hanbok.
places.tips: Guard changes at Daehanmun at 11:00, 14:00 and 15:30 (not on Mondays). Connect to Jeongdong-gil and Seoul Museum of Art.
places.image_query: Deoksugung stone wall road ginkgo autumn

places.name: Jongmyo Shrine
places.summary: UNESCO-listed royal ancestral shrine. The 101 m Jeongjeon hall reopened in 2025 after a 5-year restoration. Sparse and solemn.
places.why: Gives the same quiet, sacred feeling as Kamakura's shrines. Pairs with the Jongno-3ga pojangmacha street right outside after dark.
places.autumn_note: The forest paths are good in late Oct. Jongmyo Daeje (the royal ancestral rite) is held in May and early Nov, so not during the trip.
places.hours: About 09:00-18:00 in Feb-May and Sep-Oct. Weekdays and Sundays: timed guided entry (English tours several times a day). Saturdays: free self-guided entry.
places.cost_note: 1,000. Free in hanbok.
places.booking: Walk-up for the timed guided entry. Check the English tour times at the gate or on the royal palaces site.
places.tips: Self-guided on Saturday Oct 17 or 24. Otherwise join the English tour.

places.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
places.summary: Hillside lanes of lived-in hanok houses between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung, plus the Samcheong-dong cafe street.
places.why: The closest match to Kamakura's charming old lanes, but it is a residential neighborhood, so visit quietly.
places.autumn_note: Clear autumn days give views over the tiled roofs toward Namsan.
places.hours: Red zone (Bukchon-ro 11-gil, about 34,000 m2): tourists allowed only 10:00-17:00, enforced since Mar 1, 2025 and still in force in 2026. Orange zones (Bukchon-ro 5ga-gil, Gyedong-gil) and the yellow zone (Bukchon-ro 12-gil) have no curfew but are patrolled. Chartered tour buses have been banned on Bukchon-ro since 2026.
places.closed: Red-zone lanes are closed to sightseeing 17:00-10:00
places.cost_note: Free. Fine of up to 100,000 KRW for sightseeing in the red zone outside 10:00-17:00. This applies even to hanok-stay guests if they are judged to be sightseeing.
places.tips: Be in the 11-gil lanes between 10:00 and 17:00. No loud talk or drones, and don't photograph through gates. Hanok-stay guests should walk straight to their door at night.

places.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Street
places.summary: A tight cluster of 1920s urban hanok turned into cafes, bakeries and bars.
places.why: Feels like Kamakura's Komachi-dori with hanok: small lanes full of food. Easy to pair with Jongmyo, Changdeokgung and the Jongno-3ga tents.
places.autumn_note: Courtyard cafes and makgeolli bars are pleasant on cool nights.
places.cost_note: Free to wander. Cafes cost about 7,000-10,000 per drink.
places.tips: Weekday afternoons are calmer. At night, walk 3 minutes to the Jongno-3ga pojangmacha tents.

places.name: Seochon and Tongin Market
places.summary: Lanes west of the palace with hanok, galleries, small restaurants and Tongin Market. At Tongin, you buy brass coins (yeopjeon) to pay for a dosirak (lunchbox) at the food stalls, and the oil-tteokbokki stall is the classic snack.
places.why: A calmer, local-feeling 'old town' and the start of the Inwangsan trail. Similar in feel to Kamakura's back streets.
places.autumn_note: Combine with the Inwangsan sunset hike or Suseong-dong Valley.
places.closed: Tongin Market: many stalls closed Mondays (dosirak cafe days vary; verify)
places.cost_note: About 10,000 in coins for a dosirak lunch
places.tips: Tosokchon samgyetang is here, and so are Onjium and wine bars for dinner.

places.name: Inwangsan and Seoul Fortress Wall (sunset hike)
places.summary: Short, steep hike along the 600-year-old fortress wall to the 338 m granite summit, with views over Gyeongbokgung, Bugaksan, Namsan and the city lights.
places.why: Kamakura's hiking trails above the temples, plus the best sunset view over the city.
places.autumn_note: Sunset is about 17:55 on Oct 17 and 17:47 on Oct 24. Start up about 75 min before.
places.hours: Open daily. Night descent is fine on lit stairs, but bring a headlamp.
places.closed: Can close during dry-season fire warnings (rare in October)
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Start from Sajik Park or Seochon. Suseong-dong Valley and the Inwangsan forest trail (Inwangsan Jarak-gil) make good add-ons. Walk down into Seochon for dinner.

places.name: Bugaksan (Baegaksan) Fortress Wall trail
places.summary: Wall section behind the former presidential Blue House. It has been fully open since 2022 and no longer needs ID registration.
places.why: Quieter hike with views, history and an armed-guard past. Can be linked to the Cheong Wa Dae grounds.
places.autumn_note: Good foliage from late Oct.
places.hours: Daytime only. Entry usually closes mid-afternoon (verify on the day).
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Start at Changuimun (bus from Gyeongbokgung station). Finish via Malbawi to Samcheong-dong.

places.name: Naksan Park and Ihwa Mural Village wall walk
places.summary: Easy wall walk with a lit fortress wall at night and city views. It runs down to Heunginjimun and DDP.
places.why: The easiest night view in Seoul. Combine it with Hyehwa (Daehangno theater district) for dinner.
places.autumn_note: Cool nights are good for the 30-minute walk to DDP.
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Walk Hyehwa station → Naksan → wall → Heunginjimun → DDP after dark.
places.image_query: Naksan Park Seoul city wall night

places.name: National Museum of Korea
places.summary: Korea's flagship museum. Highlights include the 'Room of Quiet Contemplation' with two pensive bodhisattvas, Silla gold crowns and a 10-story pagoda in the hall. It set attendance records in 2025-26.
places.why: One sitting gives the whole story of Korean history and art. Like the Tokyo National Museum.
places.autumn_note: The special exhibition '우리들의 밥상' (Our Dining Table, on Korean food culture) runs Jul 1 - Oct 25, 2026, which suits food lovers.
places.hours: Since Mar 16, 2026: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun 09:30-17:30. Wed and Sat 09:30-21:00 (last entry 30 min before close).
places.closed: Jan 1, Lunar New Year, Chuseok. Open Mondays.
places.cost_note: Permanent galleries free. Special exhibitions are often 0-15,000.
places.tips: Good Monday choice when the palaces are closed. Go on Wed Oct 21 or Sat Oct 24 for the evening hours. The Ichon Hangang Park riverside is nearby.
places.image_query: National Museum of Korea pensive bodhisattva room

places.name: Leeum Museum of Art
places.summary: Samsung's museum, in buildings by Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel and Rem Koolhaas. Korean celadon, buncheong and paintings, plus contemporary art.
places.why: Pairs with Hannam-dong's boutiques and cafes, like Roppongi or Omotesando's Nezu Museum.
places.autumn_note: 'Into Another Space: Synesthetic Environments by Women Artists' runs May 5 - Nov 29, 2026.
places.cost_note: Special exhibitions up to about 20,000. The permanent collection has been free with a timed reservation (verify).
places.tips: Hangangjin station (Line 6), exit 1, about a 10-minute uphill walk.
places.image_query: Leeum Samsung Museum of Art building

places.name: War Memorial of Korea
places.summary: Large museum on the Korean War, with aircraft and armor outside. Free.
places.why: Useful context before or after a DMZ tour.
places.autumn_note: The outdoor plaza is pleasant in fall.
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Go the day before the DMZ. Mongtan (BBQ) and the Yongridan-gil restaurants are a 5-minute walk away.

places.name: Namsangol Hanok Village
places.summary: Five relocated Joseon houses with a pond garden, a time capsule and traditional-game and craft programs. Free.
places.why: A free, uncrowded hanok stop on the walk from Myeongdong up Namsan.
places.autumn_note: The pond garden turns color in late Oct.
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Walk from Chungmuro station. Continue up Namsan to N Seoul Tower on foot.

places.name: Namsan and N Seoul Tower
places.summary: TV tower on Namsan with an observatory, a love-lock terrace and Namsan's fortress wall trails.
places.why: The Tokyo Tower of Seoul. The walk up is free and the view at dusk is classic.
places.autumn_note: The Namsan circuit road (Namsan Sunhwan-ro) has strong foliage in late Oct.
places.cost_note: Observatory adult 21,000 (cheaper on Klook, Creatrip and similar). The Namsan cable car round trip was quoted at 8,500 by one source, but older sources say about 14,000-15,000 (verify). The planned Myeongdong-Namsan gondola has NOT opened: construction has been halted by lawsuits, and Seoul lost again on appeal in Sept 2026.
places.tips: Skip the paid observatory and enjoy the free terrace. Take Namsan circulator bus 01A or 01B, or walk the stairs from Namsangol.

places.name: Lotte World Tower – Seoul Sky
places.summary: Observatory on floors 117-123 of the 555 m tower, with a glass-floor Sky Deck. Seokchon Lake is at its base.
places.why: The Shibuya Sky or Tokyo Skytree equivalent: a sunset-to-night view of the whole city.
places.autumn_note: The cherry trees around Seokchon Lake turn red in late Oct.
places.cost_note: Adult 29,000 per a 2026 Korean source (some older pages say 31,000; check). Fast pass 50,000. OTAs discount it.
places.booking: Walk-up or OTA. Book a sunset slot.
places.tips: Clear autumn evenings are best. Combine with Seokchon Lake, or take the Hangang Bus from Jamsil pier.

places.name: Myeongdong
places.summary: Dense shopping streets of K-beauty stores and street-food carts in the evening. Myeongdong Cathedral and the Lotte and Shinsegae flagship department stores are here.
places.why: Shibuya-style crowd energy and neon at night. The most convenient base for the airport.
places.autumn_note: Street-food stalls (hotteok, roasted chestnuts, sweet potatoes) get busier as nights cool.
places.hours: Shops about 10:00-22:00. Street stalls from about 16:00.
places.cost_note: Street-food items about 4,000-10,000
places.tips: Myeongdong Kyoja for kalguksu. Walk to Namsan or the Shinsegae main store's media facade.

places.name: Hongdae and Yeonnam-dong (Gyeongui Line Forest Park)
places.summary: University district with busking, clubs, live music, indie shops and photo booths. Yeonnam-dong's linear park ('Yeontral Park') is lined with cafes and restaurants.
places.why: The closest match to Shibuya, Shimokitazawa and Harajuku: youth culture, street performers and late nights.
places.autumn_note: Picnics on the Gyeongui Line forest park are good in October.
places.hours: Busking from about 18:00. Clubs until dawn on weekends.
places.cost_note: Club entry about 10,000-20,000. Live clubs about 15,000-30,000.
places.tips: Friday or Saturday night is best for energy. Mangwon Market and the Han River are 15 minutes' walk.

places.name: Seongsu-dong and Seoul Forest
places.summary: Old shoe-factory district turned into Seoul's pop-up and concept-store capital (Seongsu 'Brooklyn'). Weekend pop-ups, specialty coffee, Dior Seongsu, and Seoul Forest park next door.
places.why: Like Daikanyama or Kuramae: design, cafes and pop-up culture that changes weekly.
places.autumn_note: Seoul Forest's ginkgos and metasequoias turn in late Oct to Nov. Picnic there.
places.hours: Shops about 11:00-21:00. Pop-ups busiest on weekends.
places.cost_note: Free to wander
places.booking: Some pop-ups need a Naver or Catchtable reservation
places.tips: Check Instagram for that week's pop-ups. Go Sat Oct 17 or Sat Oct 24. Ttukseom Hangang Park is close.

places.name: Gangnam / COEX Starfield Library / Bongeunsa
places.summary: COEX Mall's Starfield Library has 13 m bookshelves. The WAVE anamorphic LED screen is at the SM Town crossing. Bongeunsa, a 1,200-year-old Seon temple with a 23 m Maitreya statue, is directly across the street.
places.why: A modern 'Tokyo in Korea' contrast: glass towers next to an old temple, like Zojoji beside Tokyo Tower.
places.autumn_note: Bongeunsa's grounds turn color in late Oct. Its 'Temple Life' program (about 2 h) runs on set days.
places.cost_note: Free (Bongeunsa Temple Life is paid; check the temple's site)
places.tips: Do Bongeunsa first, then COEX. Lotte World Tower is 15 minutes away on Line 2.

places.name: Garosu-gil, Apgujeong Rodeo, Dosan Park
places.summary: A ginkgo-lined boulevard, Apgujeong Rodeo's boutiques and restaurants, and Dosan Park's flagship stores (Gentle Monster Haus Dosan and others).
places.why: An Omotesando or Aoyama analog: polished shopping and dining.
places.autumn_note: Garosu-gil literally means 'tree-lined street'. Its ginkgos go gold in late Oct to Nov.
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Link it to the Hangang Bus Apgujeong pier or the Banpo fountain at night.

places.name: Euljiro ('Hipjiro') and Nogari Alley
places.summary: Print-shop and hardware-store alleys with hidden 2nd- and 3rd-floor bars. Nogari Alley spills plastic tables into the street for cheap draft beer and dried pollock.
places.why: The Golden Gai, Yurakucho-under-the-tracks or Omoide Yokocho equivalent: gritty, retro and lively.
places.autumn_note: Outdoor tables are best on cool October evenings.
places.hours: Nogari Alley about 17:00-late. Some places close on Sundays.
places.cost_note: Beer about 4,000-6,000. Nogari about 2,000-3,000 per stick.
places.tips: The original Eulji OB Bear was evicted in 2022, but the alley lives on. Combine with the Euljiro Sewoon Plaza rooftop for a view.

places.name: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha street
places.summary: A row of orange-tent street bars on Donhwamun-ro and around Ikseon-dong serving soju, grilled fish, sea snails and stir-fries.
places.why: The night-tent bar experience, like Fukuoka yatai or a Tokyo yokocho.
places.autumn_note: Tents are best on cool October nights.
places.closed: Some tents on Sundays or in rain
places.cost_note: Dishes about 15,000-25,000. Soju about 5,000-6,000.
places.tips: Cash or card is fine at most. Pick a busy tent.

places.name: Itaewon / Hannam-dong / Haebangchon
places.summary: International bar and food scene. Hannam-dong has design-led shops and cafes, and Haebangchon is a hillside rooftop-bar village.
places.why: Like Roppongi with Ebisu: global food and cocktail bars.
places.autumn_note: Rooftop bars with a Namsan view in cool weather.
places.cost_note: Cocktails about 18,000-25,000
places.tips: Leeum is in Hannam. Crowds are now well managed (crowd-control rules since the 2022 Halloween crush). Avoid the Halloween weekend, which is after the trip anyway.

places.name: Mangwon-dong and Mangwon Market
places.summary: Neighborhood market known for croquettes, dakgangjeong (crispy sweet chicken) and cheap street food. Indie cafes are nearby, and Mangwon Hangang Park is a 10-minute walk.
places.why: Local, Shimokita-style everyday Seoul. Buy food and picnic by the river.
places.autumn_note: Picnic at Mangwon Hangang Park at sunset. Hangang Bus Mangwon pier is here.
places.tips: Get takeaway chicken and beer and walk to the river for chimaek.

places.name: Gwangjang Market
places.summary: Covered market from 1905, known for food stalls selling bindaetteok (mung-bean pancakes), yukhoe (beef tartare), mayak gimbap and kalguksu.
places.why: The Tsukiji Outer Market-style food crawl.
places.autumn_note: Hot pancakes and makgeolli suit cool evenings.
places.hours: Food stalls about 09:00-23:00. Fabric shops close earlier.
places.closed: Many non-food shops close on Sundays. Food alley open daily.
places.cost_note: About 20,000-30,000 per person for a crawl. Check prices before ordering: overcharging scandals in 2023-24 led to listed prices.
places.tips: Soonhee-ne bindaetteok and Buchon Yukhoe are the classics. Expect queues on weekend evenings.

places.name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
places.summary: Seoul's huge seafood market. You choose live fish on the ground floor, then upstairs restaurants slice it as hoe (sashimi) and make maeuntang (spicy fish stew) for a setting fee.
places.why: The direct analog to their sushi-omakase love: Korean-style sashimi, DIY and lively.
places.autumn_note: Autumn seasonal seafood: jeoneo (gizzard shad, grilled), daeha (king prawns, salt-grilled), and fat autumn flounder and rockfish.
places.hours: General fish market about 01:30-22:00. The high-end live fish section runs 24 h.
places.cost_note: About 40,000-60,000 per person for a full sashimi meal. Upstairs setting fee about 5,000-15,000 per group or per person, plus maeuntang.
places.booking: None. A guided tour (about 2-3 h) is an option for first-timers.
places.tips: Compare a few stalls and agree on price and weight. Go for dinner. It is on Line 1 and Line 9 (Noryangjin station).

places.name: Namdaemun Market
places.summary: Huge old market with galchi-jorim alley (braised hairtail) and kalguksu alley. Next to Sungnyemun gate.
places.why: A cheap, old-school eating stop near a Seoul Station or Myeongdong base.
places.autumn_note: Hairtail (galchi) is in season in autumn.
places.cost_note: Galchi-jorim about 12,000-15,000 per person
places.tips: Go on a weekday. Pair with Deoksugung and Seoullo 7017.

places.name: Jogyesa Temple
places.summary: Headquarters of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, with ancient locust and white pine trees. Insadong is next door.
places.why: A working downtown temple and the easiest temple visit in Seoul.
places.autumn_note: Jogyesa usually holds its chrysanthemum festival (시월국화향기) from mid or late Oct into Nov. The 2026 dates were not confirmed.
places.cost_note: Free. Templestay information center across the street.
places.tips: Combine with Insadong and Ssamziegil.

places.name: Haneul Park (Sky Park) – Seoul Silver Grass Festival
places.summary: A former landfill hill covered in eulalia silver grass. The 25th Seoul Silver Grass Festival (서울억새축제) is Oct 17-23, 2026, 10:00-21:00, with evening lighting.
places.why: The trip's autumn silver-grass moment inside Seoul, like Hakone Sengokuhara.
places.autumn_note: The festival dates overlap the trip almost exactly. The grass peaks mid-to-late Oct.
places.hours: Festival Oct 17-23, 10:00-21:00. Evening hours run later only during the festival.
places.cost_note: Free. The 'Maengkkongi' electric shuttle up the hill costs about 3,000 one way (verify).
places.tips: Go 1.5 h before sunset and stay for the lights. World Cup Stadium station (Line 6), then cross the footbridge and climb 291 stairs. Can be combined with Mangwon and Hongdae.

places.name: Han River parks (Yeouido, Banpo, Ttukseom) and chimaek
places.summary: Riverside parks for evening picnics with delivered fried chicken and beer (chimaek). Banpo Bridge has the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, and you can rent bikes. The Hangang Bus links the piers.
places.why: A uniquely Seoul evening ritual and the city's big-river breathing space.
places.autumn_note: October is the best month for river picnics. The Banpo fountain season normally ends Oct 31. Shows are usually 12:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:30, 21:00 (20 min each, based on 2025 pattern; verify).
places.cost_note: Delivered chicken about 22,000-28,000 per bird. Bikes about 3,000 per hour.
places.booking: Order chicken through Coupang Eats or Baemin to a 'delivery zone' (배달존), or buy at the convenience stores in the park.
places.tips: Banpo for the fountain. Yeouido for the biggest lawn. Ttukseom near Seongsu.

places.name: Hangang Bus (Han River water bus)
places.area: Magok – Mangwon – Yeouido – Apgujeong – Oksu – Ttukseom – Jamsil
places.summary: River commuter ferry launched Sept 18, 2025. It was partly suspended in late 2025 (groundings), then resumed in 2026. 603,293 riders by Sept 2026 and 99.3% on time in July 2026. Seoul plans 15-minute intervals, express and cross-river routes.
places.why: A cheap, scenic river cruise between neighborhoods, like a Sumida River water bus.
places.autumn_note: Late-afternoon sailings give river sunsets.
places.time_needed: Yeouido-Jamsil about 75 min. Full Magok-Jamsil about 2 h (verify).
places.hours: One 2026 source listed Jamsil→Yeouido departures 10:00-17:30 and Magok→Yeouido 10:20-17:40, daily. Check the current timetable on hgbus.co.kr before going.
places.closed: Suspended in fog, high water or strong wind
places.cost_note: Adult 3,000. Covered by the Climate Card (기후동행카드) for an add-on fee (verify for the short-term tourist card).
places.booking: Walk-up with a T-money or credit card. Seating is limited (about 199 seats), so arrive early on weekends.
places.tips: Ride Yeouido → Apgujeong or Ttukseom to link the parks with Garosu-gil or Seongsu.

places.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream and Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
places.summary: An 11 km restored urban stream walk from Cheonggye Plaza east, ending at Zaha Hadid's DDP with its night LED rose garden or light shows and the late-night Dongdaemun fashion malls.
places.why: A free night walk through the city, similar to Shibuya's mix of design and nightlife.
places.autumn_note: The Seoul Lantern Festival on Cheonggyecheon is usually Nov-Dec, so it falls after the trip.
places.hours: 24 h. The DDP building is about 10:00-20:00.
places.cost_note: Free. DDP exhibitions are paid.
places.tips: Walk from Gwanghwamun to Gwangjang Market along the stream.

places.name: Hanbok rental near Gyeongbokgung
places.summary: Dozens of rental shops near Gyeongbokgung station and Anguk. Hairstyling and accessories are extra.
places.why: Like a yukata or kimono rental in Kamakura or Kyoto. It also gets you into all palaces and Jongmyo free.
places.autumn_note: Autumn colors make for strong palace photos. Cool weather is comfortable in the layers.
places.cost_note: About 15,000-30,000 for 2-4 h basic. Premium 40,000-70,000. Hair about 5,000-15,000.
places.booking: Walk-in, or book on Creatrip, Klook or Naver for discounts
places.tips: Return times are strict. Choose a shop near the palace you will visit.

places.name: Jjimjilbang: SPAREX Dongdaemun
places.summary: 24-hour jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse and sauna) with gender-separated baths, themed sauna rooms and a shared lounge. It is the most central 24 h option now that Dragon Hill Spa, Itaewon Land and Siloam at Seoul Station have closed.
places.why: The bathhouse culture that onsen lovers will enjoy. The atmosphere is urban, not nature.
places.autumn_note: Good after a cold night walk.
places.cost_note: About 14,000 (Feb 2026). Extra charge overnight.
places.tips: Tattoo rules are relaxed compared with Japan. Bathing is nude and gender-separated. The shared lounge needs the provided clothes.

places.name: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (day trip)
places.summary: UNESCO-listed 1796 fortress with a 5.7 km wall loop, gates, Banghwasuryujeong pavilion and the rebuilt Hwaseong Haenggung palace. Haenggung-dong has cafes and the famous Suwon galbi.
places.why: A 'Kamakura-like' heritage day out from the capital: a walkable wall town with good food.
places.autumn_note: The Hwaseong Cultural Festival (Oct 4-11, 2026) and the media art event (to Oct 6) END before arrival. Foliage on the wall around Paldalsan is good late Oct.
places.hours: Haenggung about 09:00-18:00. The wall is open all the time.
places.cost_note: Fortress about 1,000 + Haenggung 1,500-2,000 (verify). Flying Suwon balloon about 20,000 and the Hwaseong trolley about 4,000 (2025-era prices, verify).
places.tips: Subway Line 1 from Seoul Station to Suwon is about 1 h. ITX or Mugunghwa trains take about 30 min. Bus 3000 runs from Gangnam. Suwon galbi: Bon Suwon Galbi or Yeonpo Galbi.

places.name: DMZ tour (Imjingak, 3rd Tunnel, Dora Observatory)
places.summary: Licensed group tours to Imjingak, the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory and Dorasan station. JSA (Panmunjom) civilian tours have been suspended since July 2023. Only special-category groups resumed, and general public and foreigner JSA tours are NOT running as of 2026.
places.why: A history counterweight to the trip.
places.autumn_note: Clear October skies give the best views from Dora Observatory.
places.hours: Tours depart about 07:00-08:00 from central Seoul
places.closed: Mondays (the 3rd Tunnel closes; some tours swap in the 2nd Tunnel). Also national holidays or military situations.
places.cost_note: Standard DMZ tours about 55,000-95,000 per person. Be wary of anything sold as 'JSA'; some substitute a JSA museum.
places.booking: Book 1+ week ahead via Klook, Viator, GetYourGuide or Creatrip. Passport required on the day.
places.tips: Go Tue-Sat. Avoid tours that promise JSA. Pairs with the War Memorial.

places.name: Nami Island + Garden of Morning Calm (Gapyeong day trip)
places.summary: Nami Island is a tree-lined river island, famous for its metasequoia and ginkgo lanes and the K-drama 'Winter Sonata'. The Garden of Morning Calm (37.7440, 127.3530) is a large garden in the hills.
places.why: Autumn foliage in a nature setting, an easy rail trip from Seoul.
places.autumn_note: Ginkgo and metasequoia lanes usually peak late Oct to early Nov. It is very crowded on weekends.
places.cost_note: Nami admission including the ferry about 16,000. Garden about 11,000-12,000. ITX-Cheongchun Yongsan or Cheongnyangni → Gapyeong about 8,000-9,600 one way (verify).
places.booking: Walk-up. Weekday ITX seats via Korail (letskorail.com).
places.tips: Go on a weekday. Taxi from Gapyeong station to Nami wharf about 5 min. The zipwire is optional (about 50,000).

places.name: Bukhansan National Park – Baegundae Peak
places.summary: Highest point in Seoul (836 m), a granite summit with steel cables and rails and a 360-degree view. The Bukhansanseong mountain-fortress route passes old gates and temples.
places.why: Big-nature hike from a subway line. The Izu or Hakone outdoors feel without leaving Seoul.
places.autumn_note: 2026 forecasts give first color around Oct 15-18 and peak about Oct 28 - Nov 1. The upper slopes should be colorful during the trip, and the lower valleys turn as the week goes on.
places.hours: Trails close about 2 h before sunset (entry cut-off around 14:00-15:00 in late October; verify)
places.cost_note: Free
places.tips: Bus 704 or 34 from Gupabal station (Line 3) to the Bukhansanseong entrance. Wear grippy shoes because the top has exposed granite with cables. Avoid weekends.

lodging.name: Rakkojae Seoul
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol (heated floor) rooms with futon bedding. The larger rooms sleep 3. Confirm a 3-person room when booking.
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. HotelsCombined (Oct 2026) shows about US$435 average and from about US$248 per night for 2 guests. Expect a surcharge for a 3rd person and higher weekend rates. Breakfast included. A mud-sauna or bath experience and dinner are add-ons.
lodging.highlights: The ryokan analog: a 130-year-old restored hanok with a courtyard, traditional breakfast and service. Walking distance to Changdeokgung, Bukchon and Ikseon-dong.
lodging.drawbacks: Expensive. Thin walls, and shared or small bathrooms in some rooms. Sits on Gyedong-gil (Bukchon orange zone), so expect quiet rules at night.
lodging.booking: Direct (rkj.co.kr; the site has a certificate error) or OTAs. Foreigners can book.

lodging.name: Chiwoonjung (luxury hanok)
lodging.room_for_3: Exclusive-use hanok house with separate rooms
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE from earlier-year rates. Not verified for Oct 2026.
lodging.highlights: Designer high-end hanok and one of the closest things to a top ryokan in Seoul, with a whole house to yourselves.
lodging.drawbacks: Very expensive for the budget. No onsen. Bukchon nighttime quiet rules apply.
lodging.booking: Direct or Mr & Mrs Smith-type OTAs

lodging.name: Bukchon or Seochon hanok guesthouse (registered, e.g. via Hanok Stay listings)
lodging.room_for_3: Ondol family room for 3-4 on floor bedding, or a whole small house
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. Typical OTA range for a 3-person hanok room or small house in Oct. Book only listings with a business registration number.
lodging.drawbacks: Quality varies. Shared bathrooms in some. Only legally registered stays are bookable in 2026.

lodging.name: Somerset Palace Seoul
lodging.room_for_3: 2-bedroom serviced apartment with kitchen and washer
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. HotelsCombined (Oct 2026) shows studios and 1-bedrooms from about US$69-221 (avg about US$191) for 2 guests. 2-bedroom units usually price around 1.7-2.2x a studio.
lodging.highlights: Best location for the palaces: walk to Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon, Insadong and Ikseon. Two bedrooms and a laundry, and rated 8.8.
lodging.drawbacks: Older interiors. The Myeongdong airport limousine stop is 2 km away, or take AREX to Seoul Station and then a taxi.

lodging.name: Orakai Insadong Suites
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. Not verified for Oct 2026 because the search budget ran out.
lodging.highlights: Walk to Ikseon-dong, Jongno-3ga tents, Jongmyo and Changdeokgung. Space for 3.

lodging.name: Fraser Place Central Seoul
lodging.area: Seodaemun / Tongil-ro 78 (about 10 min from Seoul Station)
lodging.room_for_3: Two Bedrooms Deluxe or Super Deluxe serviced residence. One Bedroom Super Deluxe Family is also an option.
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. HotelsCombined Oct 10-11, 2026 shows US$108-330 by category (avg about US$297) for 2 guests. 2-bedroom units are at the top of that range or above.
lodging.highlights: Kitchen and laundry. Easy airport access via AREX (Seoul Station) or a taxi. Walk to Deoksugung and Gwanghwamun.
lodging.drawbacks: Big-city business area. Fewer restaurants right outside at night.

lodging.name: Nine Tree by Parnas Seoul Myeongdong 2
lodging.name_ko: 나인트리 바이 파르나스 서울 명동 II
lodging.room_for_3: Family room (one double + one single, listed among amenities) or 2 rooms
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. HotelsCombined Oct 12-13, 2026: standard rooms from about US$93-112, queen about US$170, premier about US$193 (2 guests). A family room or 2 standard rooms comes to about 230,000-380,000 KRW.

lodging.name: Oakwood Premier Coex Center

lodging.highlights: 5-star with indoor pool and sauna. Linked to COEX, Starfield Library and Bongeunsa. The airport limousine stops at COEX.

lodging.name: Courtyard by Marriott Seoul Namdaemun
lodging.area: Namdaemun / near Seoul Station and Myeongdong
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE for 2 rooms. Not verified for Oct 2026.
lodging.highlights: Rooftop view of Sungnyemun. 10-minute walk or short taxi to Seoul Station (AREX). Marriott points.

lodging.name: Mercure Ambassador Seoul Hongdae
lodging.price_note: ESTIMATE. Not verified for Oct 2026. AREX all-stop trains run straight from ICN to Hongik Univ. station (about 50 min).
lodging.highlights: Nightlife base with the Shibuya-like energy. Direct AREX link. Mangwon, Yeonnam and Haneul Park are close.
lodging.drawbacks: Noisy streets. Far from the palaces (about 25 min).

food.booking: Catchtable. Hard to get. Price approximate.

Mongtan (straw-fired galbi, Korean BBQ)

Already over before arrival (do not plan around these)

tips: Where to base: Jongno (Anguk, Insadong, Jongno 3-ga, Ikseon-dong) is the best single base for these travelers. You can walk to Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Jongmyo, Bukchon, Ikseon-dong, Gwangjang and the Jongno-3ga or Euljiro nightlife. Book 1-2 nights in a Bukchon hanok (Rakkojae) as the ryokan analog, then move to a 2-bedroom serviced residence (Somerset Palace) or a Myeongdong/Euljiro hotel. If they want nightlife over culture, base at Hongdae instead, which has a direct AREX all-stop train.

For the 05:15 Saturday arrival: AREX or a limousine bus runs from about 05:15-05:40. Booking the Oct 16 night means the room is ready at 07:00. Otherwise leave bags at the hotel or at Seoul Station lockers or T-Luggage and start at Gwangjang or Noryangjin for breakfast (Noryangjin's live section runs 24 h).

Plan around closing days. MONDAY Oct 19: Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung, Leeum, the War Memorial and Namsangol are closed, and DMZ tours skip the 3rd Tunnel. Good Monday picks are the National Museum, Gyeongbokgung, Jongmyo, Noryangjin, Seongsu or a Suwon/Nami day trip. TUESDAY Oct 20: Gyeongbokgung and Jongmyo are closed.
Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden online 6 days ahead at 10:00 KST (21:00 US Eastern the evening before). Autumn slots sell out in minutes. On-site tickets go on sale at opening.
Hanbok means free entry to all palaces and Jongmyo, which saves 1,000-3,000 each. The bigger value is the photos in autumn colors.

Seoul foliage timing: 2026 forecasts put Bukhansan's first color around Oct 15-18 and the peak around Oct 28 - Nov 1. In the city the palace ginkgos peak late Oct to early Nov. Expect early-to-mid color on Oct 17-24. Silver grass (Haneul Park) is at its best then.
Sunset is about 17:55 on Oct 17 and about 17:47 on Oct 24. Time the Inwangsan hike, Seoul Sky and Haneul Park around it.
Get a T-money or WOWPASS card on arrival, and install Naver Map (Google Maps walking directions are poor in Korea), Kakao T (taxis), Catchtable (restaurant bookings) and Papago (translation).

Budget sketch for the Seoul portion: about 250,000-450,000 KRW per night for 3 in a mid-range triple or 2-bedroom. Paid sights are cheap (palaces 1,000-3,000; Secret Garden 8,000; Seoul Sky about 29,000; N Seoul Tower 21,000; DMZ tour about 75,000; Starlight Tour 60,000).

Airbnb and short-term rentals: since 2026, unregistered listings can no longer be booked, and Airbnb requires a business registration number. Only 'foreign-tourist urban homestay' (외국인관광 도시민박업, host must live on site), hanok-experience businesses and licensed lodging are legal. Officetel 'apartments' are illegal and risk last-minute cancellation. Prefer hotels, serviced residences and registered hanok stays.
warnings: JSA / Panmunjom is NOT open to general or foreign civilian tours as of 2026 (suspended since July 2023). Only special-category groups resumed. Treat any 'DMZ + JSA' tour sold to foreigners with suspicion. Standard DMZ tours run Tue-Sun.
Closed for good: Dragon Hill Spa (Yongsan), Itaewon Land (site being redeveloped) and Siloam Sauna at Seoul Station (moved to Gwangjin-gu). Use SPAREX Dongdaemun or Dongmyo (24 h, about 14,000).

The Namsan gondola (Myeongdong to N Seoul Tower), promised for spring 2026, is NOT open. Construction has been halted for about 2 years, and Seoul lost again on appeal in Sept 2026. Use the old cable car, circulator buses 01A/01B or the stairs.

Bukchon red zone (Bukchon-ro 11-gil): sightseeing only 10:00-17:00, fine up to 100,000 KRW. It applies to hanok-stay guests too if they are judged to be sightseeing. Tour buses are banned on Bukchon-ro from 2026.
The Gyeongbokgung Starlight Tour foreigner sessions (Oct 21-24) were listed SOLD OUT on Creatrip on Oct 6. The Changdeokgung Moonlight Tour ends Oct 17, and its foreigner sessions have ended.
Palace fees: an increase is announced for Jan 2027 and does not affect October 2026.
The Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival (Oct 4-11) and Media Art (to Oct 6) end before arrival.

Hangang Bus: running, but the timetable has changed several times since its 2025 launch (partial suspension, then resumption in March 2026). Confirm on hgbus.co.kr the day before. Sailings can be cancelled in fog.
